name: ping
title: Test network connectivity with ping
summary: Tests whether a remote host can be reached and measures basic response time using ICMP echo requests.

examples.description: Tests connectivity to a public IP address without relying on DNS.
Tests connectivity and confirms whether the hostname can be resolved.
Sends echo requests continuously until the command is stopped with Ctrl+C.
Forces the command to use IPv4.

permissions.notes: Standard ping tests normally do not require administrator access.

risk.warning: Ping does not modify the system. Some hosts or firewalls may block ICMP traffic, so a failed test does not always mean the destination is offline.

output_fields.name: Reply from
output_fields.description: Shows the address of the device that responded.

output_fields.name: Bytes
output_fields.description: Shows the size of the ICMP response.

output_fields.name: Time
output_fields.description: Shows the round-trip response time in milliseconds.

output_fields.name: TTL
output_fields.description: Shows the remaining Time to Live value in the response packet.

output_fields.name: Packets sent, received, and lost
output_fields.description: Summarizes whether packets reached the destination and returned.

output_fields.name: Minimum, maximum, and average
output_fields.description: Summarizes round-trip timing across the completed tests.

common_errors.meaning: No ICMP reply was received before the timeout. The destination may be unavailable, unreachable, or blocking ping traffic.
A local device or router could not find a valid route to the destination.

common_errors.message: Ping request could not find host
common_errors.meaning: The hostname could not be resolved. Check spelling and DNS configuration.
The local system could not send the request, often because of an adapter, routing, or TCP/IP configuration problem.
